pins.advancedHint: Pin rows with a label and a colour; see what sets them apart
pins.intro: Pin rows you want to keep an eye on (test orders, suspected frauds…) with a label and a colour. Then see what distinguishes them from the other rows, or turn the labels into a column in Clean.
pins.rowsInvalid: Row numbers as shown, separated by commas; a range like 40-45 (500 rows at most).
pins.selected: {count} selected in the table, plus the rows typed here.
pins.label: Label
pins.labelExisting: Existing label ({rows} rows): the rows join it.
pins.labelNew: A new label. A row has one label: pinning it again changes it.
pins.lostOne: 1 pinned row was not found after the last import (R-PIN-02): it is left out of the comparison and of the column.
pins.lostMany: {count} pinned rows were not found after the last import (R-PIN-02): they are left out of the comparison and of the column.
pins.dataHint: Click row numbers in the table to select rows.
pins.unusualHint: Tick rows in the table above to select them.
pins.cleanHint: Row numbers as the Data page shows them.
pins.compare.title: What distinguishes pinned rows
pins.compare.loading: Comparing the pinned rows with the others
pins.compare.scope: {pinned} pinned rows against the {others} other rows of the dataset, on {columns} columns (numbers and categories). Filters do not apply.
pins.compare.rules: Rules that describe the pinned rows
pins.compare.ruleRows: {rows} pinned rows · {share} % of the rows it matches are pinned
